status_observed: 200 application/json, body `[]` -- when `format=pdf` was requested and a PDF file was expected
what_is_wrong: The `format=pdf|excel` export branch is unreachable for any login that has no linked Employee record. The handler returns the bare JSON list `[]` at an early return before the `if format:` export block is evaluated, so the caller receives 200 application/json instead of the PDF/XLSX attachment the contract promises. Every other export-capable endpoint in the module honours `format` unconditionally, so a client that requests an export and branches on content-type (or triggers a file download) silently gets JSON from this one endpoint only.
evidence:
Controlled comparison, same endpoint, same query, two different logins:

(a) As employee@meshrd.in (HAS a linked Employee record, 4 timesheet rows):
    Request:  GET http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/v1/timesheets/me?format=pdf
    Response: HTTP 200
              content-type:        application/pdf
              content-disposition: attachment; filename="My_Timesheet.pdf"
              2634 bytes, body starts b'%PDF-1.4\n%\x93\x8c\x8b\x9e ReportLab Generated PDF document (opensource)'
    GET .../timesheets/me?format=excel -> 200, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, filename="My_Timesheet.xlsx", 5232 bytes, b'PK\x03\x04'

(b) As superadmin@meshrd.in (NO linked Employee record -- users.id 8ea8f1e1-7439-49f1-8bd4-027e7f005c14 has no employees row with that user_id):
    Request:  GET http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/v1/timesheets/me?format=pdf
    Response: HTTP 200
              content-type:        application/json
              content-disposition: (absent)
              2 bytes, body `[]`
    GET .../timesheets/me?format=excel -> 200, application/json, 2 bytes, `[]`   (identical -- format ignored entirely)
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/projects.py:1214-1216 -- `own_id = await org_scope.get_own_employee_id(db, current_user)` / `if own_id is None: return []`. This early return precedes the `if format:` export branch at app/api/v1/projects.py:1228, so the export path is skipped instead of exporting an empty result set.

what_is_wrong: `mode` (L1) and the values in `fields` (L3) are written straight to the database with no validation against the allowed enum. An out-of-range value violates the MySQL CHECK constraint (ck_role_perm_mode / ck_rpf_mode) and surfaces as an unhandled 500. Note the same handler DOES validate screen_key properly (422), so this is an inconsistent gap rather than a deliberate choice. The transaction rolls back atomically, so no data corruption results â€” but a user-supplied value should not produce a 500.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/rbac_admin.py:219 (`row.mode = change.mode`) and :256-262 (field mode) have no membership check; the constraint is only in alembic/versions/0001_platform_core.py:248 (ck_role_perm_mode) and :290 (ck_rpf_mode).

status_observed: 201 with override_value stored verbatim as "bogus_value"; the value then appears as the effective screen mode in GET /api/v1/me
what_is_wrong: `override_value` is never validated â€” not by the API and not by the DB (VARCHAR(20), no CHECK constraint, unlike layer which has ck_upo_layer). An L1/L4 override_value is assigned directly to the effective permission mode by the resolver, so a typo'd or junk value becomes the user's screen mode. Because every downstream visibility test is `mode != "none"`, a junk value silently makes an otherwise-hidden screen VISIBLE. This is a security-relevant fail-open, not just cosmetic.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/rbac_admin.py:398-401 stores body.override_value with no allowlist check; app/rbac/resolver.py:215 and :224 then do `mode = ov.override_value` unconditionally. DB column has no CHECK (alembic/versions/0001_platform_core.py:322).

status_observed: 200 OK â€” the bogus key is written to role_permission_actions / role_permission_fields and logged to the change log
what_is_wrong: Unknown `action_key` values in `actions` and unknown `field_key` values in `fields` are silently accepted and persisted as new permission rows, plus a PermissionChangeLog entry. An unknown `screen_key` in the same request body is correctly rejected with 422, so this is an inconsistent validation gap. The junk rows are invisible in GET /rbac/matrix (which builds its action/field list from the screen registry, not from the stored rows), so an operator typo silently creates unreachable, un-auditable permission rows that no UI can ever see or remove.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/rbac_admin.py:238-249 (actions loop) and :256-267 (fields loop) never check the key against ScreenAction / ScreenSensitiveField for that screen, unlike the screen_key check at :196-198 and unlike POST /rbac/overrides which DOES validate both (rbac_admin.py:386-393).
